lines.text: There are over two hundred wild hippos in Colombia.
And one man put them there.
He grew up in Medellín, the son of a farmer and a schoolteacher.
As a teenager, he sold fake lottery tickets and smuggled cigarettes.
By his twenties, he was smuggling something far worse.
Cocaine.
By the planeload.
His cartel supplied an estimated eighty percent of what reached the United States.
Forbes put him on its billionaires list seven years in a row.
His brother said they spent two and a half thousand dollars a month on rubber bands, just to wrap the cash.
He built a ranch with a private zoo.
Giraffes, zebras, and four hippos.
He was even elected to Colombia's Congress.
But it was all built on blood.
Bombings.
A passenger plane blown out of the sky.
Thousands dead.
He surrendered to a prison he built for himself, then walked right out of it.
In 1993, police cornered him on a Medellín rooftop.
He was killed one day after his forty-fourth birthday.
His name was Pablo Escobar.
His empire died with him.
The hippos didn't.
